definition_zh: v. 剥夺；使丧失；夺去（所需或应有的东西）
definition_en: to take something needed or wanted away from someone, or to prevent them having it
core_image: 孩子手中的书被抽走，桌上只剩空位；供水管被关掉，水龙头一滴不出
scene: 战争让孩子们失去了上学的机会。The war deprived children of schooling.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deprived 指剥夺；句意是战争让孩子们失去了上学的机会。

senses.title: Take away something needed
senses.definition: to take away something that someone needs or has a right to
senses.definitionCN: 拿走某人需要或有权拥有的东西
senses.example: The war deprived children of schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 战争让孩子们失去了上学的机会。
senses.why: A book pulled out of a small hand.
senses.whyCN: 一本从小手里被抽走的书。

senses.title: Prevent from having
senses.definition: to prevent someone from having or doing something
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某人拥有或做某事
senses.example: The injury deprived him of a season.
senses.exampleCN: 伤病让他整整一个赛季无法上场。
senses.why: A closed tap with a dry pipe behind it.
senses.whyCN: 一个关死的龙头，后面是干管子。

senses.title: Leave in want
senses.definition: to leave a person or place without the basic things needed
senses.definitionCN: 让一个人或地方缺少基本所需
senses.example: The drought deprived the valley of water.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱使整个山谷缺水。
senses.why: An empty shelf in a village shop.
senses.whyCN: 乡村商店里一个空货架。

intro.en: Deprive comes from Latin deprivare, de- plus privare, to take away, from privus, single or one own.
intro.cn: deprive 源自拉丁语 deprivare，由 de- 加 privare（拿走）构成，privare 来自 privus（单个的、独有的）。

items.en: Privus meant single or one own.
items.cn: privus 意为单个的、自己独有的。

items.en: Privare meant to take away from.
items.cn: privare 意为从…拿走。

items.en: Deprivare meant to deprive completely.
items.cn: deprivare 意为彻底剥夺。

items.en: Deprive entered English for taking away a right.
items.cn: 十四世纪 deprive 以夺去权利义进入英语。

items.en: It widened to withholding anything needed.
items.cn: 十六世纪扩展到扣住任何所需之物。

items.en: Deprived now also describes poor areas.
items.cn: 如今 deprived 也用来描述贫困地区。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the priv- own family; the near-meaning group names other ways of taking something away.
note.cn: 形近组共享 priv-（私有）家族；近义组是其他「拿走」的说法。

entries.definition: The state of lacking basic necessities.
Belonging to one person, not the public.
A special right granted to a person or group.
To take something from someone unlawfully.
To take away rights or possessions.
To refuse to allow someone to have something.

normalIntro.en: Deprive is de- fully plus priv- own: take away what was someone own until they are without it.
normalIntro.cn: deprive 就是 de-（彻底）加 priv-（私有）：把原本属于某人的东西拿走，直到他一无所有。

normal.en: Priv- means own, as in private.
normal.cn: priv- 意为私有，如 private。

normal.en: De- means completely.
normal.cn: de- 表示彻底。

normal.en: Deprive always takes of.
normal.cn: deprive 后面总接 of。

normal.en: Deprive him of sleep means keep him awake.
normal.cn: deprive him of sleep 就是让他睡不着。

normal.en: A deprived area lacks basic services.
normal.cn: deprived 地区缺少基本服务。

abstract.en: A book pulled out of a small hand.
abstract.cn: 一本从小手里被抽走的书。

abstract.en: A closed tap with a dry pipe behind it.
abstract.cn: 一个关死的龙头，后面是干管子。

abstract.en: An empty shelf in a village shop.
abstract.cn: 乡村商店里一个空货架。

examples.en: Noise deprived her of sleep for a week.
examples.cn: 噪音让她一周没睡好。

examples.en: They are depriving the town of its library.
examples.cn: 他们正在夺走镇上的图书馆。

examples.en: The rule deprives workers of a break.
examples.cn: 这条规定让工人没有休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: deprive 谐音「弟普赖夫」——不如记 de（彻底）＋ priv（单个、私有，与 private 同根 privus）＝把私有的东西彻底拿走，「剥夺」。

root: 拉丁语 privus（单个、独有）→ privare（拿走）→ de-＋privare → deprivare → 英语 deprive

sensesIntro.en: One thing taken away: a book, a season and a shelf of goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一样被拿走的东西：一本书、一个赛季与一货架商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book pulled out of a small hand, leaving an empty place on the desk
core.cn: 核心意象：一本书从小手里被抽走，桌上只剩一个空位

branches.en: A book pulled out of a small hand.
branches.cn: 一本从小手里被抽走的书。

branches.en: A closed tap with a dry pipe behind it.

branches.en: An empty shelf in a village shop.

branches.cn: 两者都让一个地方或一个人陷入匮乏。

intro.en: Deprive is de- plus priv-; the own root builds the private and privilege family.
intro.cn: deprive 由 de- 加 priv- 构成；私有这个词根造出私人与特权一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin privus means one own, privare to take away and lex law.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 privus 意为独有，privare 意为拿走，lex 意为法律。

definition_zh: 副手；代理人；议员
definition_en: a person second in rank who acts for a leader, or an elected lawmaker in some countries
core_image: 一把椅子略微靠后，坐着的人随时准备在主人起身时接替
scene: 会议开始前，主管的位置还空着，旁边的人把文件翻到同一页。The deputy took charge while the manager was away.
sceneCN: 这里 deputy 指「副手」（第 1 个义项：位次仅次于领导、可代其行事的人）；句意是经理不在时副手接管了工作。

senses.title: Second in command
senses.definition: a person ranked just below a leader and able to act for them
senses.definitionCN: 位次仅次于领导、可以代其行事的人
senses.example: The deputy took charge while the manager was away.
senses.exampleCN: 经理不在时副手接管了工作。
senses.why: A second chair exists so that the first is never empty.
senses.whyCN: 第二把椅子的存在，是为了第一把永不空着。

senses.title: An elected lawmaker
senses.definition: a person elected to a lawmaking body in some countries
senses.definitionCN: 在某些国家被选入立法机构的人
senses.example: The deputies debated the new law for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 议员们就新法律辩论了几个小时。
senses.why: A lawmaker also acts for the people who sent him.
senses.whyCN: 议员同样替把他送去的人行事。

intro.en: Deputy came through French deputé from Latin deputare, to assign or count as belonging to a task.
intro.cn: deputy 经法语 deputé 来自拉丁语 deputare，意为指派或算作某项任务的人。

items.en: Deputare meant to assign or to count as belonging to a task.
items.cn: deputare 意为指派，或算作某项任务的人。

items.en: Deputé named a person sent to act for another.
items.cn: deputé 指被派去替别人行事的人。

items.en: English took deputy for one who acts in another's place.
items.cn: 英语借来 deputy，指代替他人行事的人。

items.en: The word spread to elected members of parliaments.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到了议会里经选举产生的成员。

items.en: Now it also appears in job titles such as deputy manager.
items.cn: 如今它也出现在副经理这类职位名称里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deput- stem, and the meaning group gives three people who stand in for another.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deput- 词干，近义组则给出三种替别人站位的人。

entries.definition: to give a task or power to another
entries.definitionCN: 把任务或权力交给别人

entries.definition: to act for someone in their absence
entries.definitionCN: 在某人不在时代其行事

entries.definition: a group sent to speak for others
entries.definitionCN: 被派去替他人说话的一组人

entries.definition: a person who helps someone with work
a person or thing used instead of another
entries.definitionCN: 用来替代另一人或物的东西

entries.definition: a person chosen to speak for a group
entries.definitionCN: 被选出来替群体说话的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a chair set slightly back and end with a hall where hands are counted.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一张稍稍靠后的椅子开始，落到一个数人头的会场。

normal.en: A deputy is a spare key that is always cut.
normal.cn: 副手就是一把随时配好的备用钥匙。

normal.en: The chair behind the leader is not a decoration.
normal.cn: 领导身后那把椅子，不是摆设。

normal.en: Deputy and deputize share the idea of being sent.
normal.cn: deputy 与 deputize 都带着被派出去的意思。

normal.en: A deputy speaks with the leader's voice but not the leader's name.
normal.cn: 副手用领导的声音说话，却不用领导的名字。

normal.en: In some parliaments, a deputy is simply a member with a vote.
normal.cn: 在某些议会里，deputy 就是有投票权的成员。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding a folder one seat to the left.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把文件夹往左推了一个座位。

abstract.en: Picture two name cards on one desk, one slightly smaller.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌上摆着两张名牌，其中一张略小。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand in a hall full of raised hands.
abstract.cn: 想象满是会举手的大厅里，又举起一只手。

examples.en: The deputy took charge while the manager was away.
examples.cn: 经理不在时副手接管了工作。

examples.en: The deputies debated the new law for hours.
examples.cn: 议员们就新法律辩论了几个小时。

examples.en: She acted as deputy during the long meeting.
examples.cn: 那场漫长的会议期间，她代理了职务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deputy 记成「代替办事的人」：de 有代的意思，put 像「派」，领导不在，被派去代替办事的，就是副手。

root: 来自法语 deputé，源头是拉丁语 deputare（指派、算作某任务的人）。它先指被派去替别人行事的人，十五世纪进入英语；十七世纪又指议会里经选举产生的成员，现代常见于副职头衔。

sensesIntro.en: From the chair just behind the leader to a seat in a parliament.
sensesIntro.cn: 从领导身后那张椅子，到议会里的一个席位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair set slightly back, its folder already open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张稍稍靠后的椅子，文件夹已经翻开。

branches.en: The first sense is a rank that waits one step behind.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是站在一步之后的位次。

branches.en: The second sense is a lawmaker who stands for voters.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是替选民站位的立法者。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of speaking for someone else.
branches.cn: 两个义项都带着替别人说话的意思。

branches.en: In an office, the word measures nearness to power.
branches.cn: 在办公室里，这个词衡量的是与权力的距离。

branches.en: In a parliament, it measures a seat won by votes.
branches.cn: 在议会里，它衡量的是一个靠选票赢来的席位。

intro.en: Deputy grows a small family of assigning and standing in, from the verb to the abstract noun.
intro.cn: deputy 长出一小族表示指派与代行的词，从动词一直到抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin deputare, to assign, from putare, to reckon or think.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 deputare（指派），再往上是 putare（估算、认为）。

definition_zh: adj. 被抛弃的；废弃的；玩忽职守的 n. 遗弃物；落魄者
definition_en: abandoned and in poor condition, or shamefully neglectful of a duty; an abandoned thing or person
core_image: 一栋厂房窗玻璃碎了一半，屋里堆着旧机器；值班表上那一格始终空着
scene: 那栋废弃的厂房被改成了画廊。The derelict factory became a gallery.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：derelict 指被抛弃的、废弃的；句意是那栋废弃厂房被改成了画廊。

pos.zh: 被抛弃的；废弃的；玩忽职守的

senses.title: Abandoned and decaying
senses.definition: left empty and falling into ruin
senses.definitionCN: 被丢空而日渐破败
senses.example: The derelict factory became a gallery.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋废弃厂房被改成了画廊。
senses.why: Half the window glass gone from a mill.
senses.whyCN: 一座厂房窗玻璃碎了一半。

senses.title: Neglectful of duty
senses.definition: shamefully failing to do what a duty requires
senses.definitionCN: 可耻地没有做到职责要求的事
senses.example: The officer was derelict in his duty.
senses.exampleCN: 那名官员玩忽职守。
senses.why: An empty square on a duty roster.
senses.whyCN: 值班表上一格空白。

senses.title: An abandoned thing or person
senses.definition: a thing left behind, or a person with no home or support
senses.definitionCN: 被丢下的东西，或无家无靠的人
senses.example: The tide left a derelict on the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水在沙滩上留下一件遗弃物。
senses.why: A hull sitting on the sand at low tide.
senses.whyCN: 低潮时坐在沙上的一具船壳。

intro.en: Derelict comes from Latin derelictus, the participle of derelinquere, to abandon completely.
intro.cn: derelict 源自拉丁语 derelictus，是 derelinquere（彻底抛弃）的分词。

items.en: Linquere meant to leave.
items.cn: linquere 意为留下、离开。

items.en: Relinquere meant to leave behind.
items.cn: relinquere 意为丢下。

items.en: Derelinquere meant to abandon completely.
items.cn: derelinquere 意为彻底抛弃。

items.en: Derelictus meant abandoned.
items.cn: derelictus 意为被抛弃的。

items.en: Derelict entered English for abandoned property.
items.cn: 十七世纪 derelict 以被弃财产义进入英语。

items.en: It also named a person neglecting duty.
items.cn: 十九世纪也指玩忽职守的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the linqu- leaving family; the near-meaning group names other kinds of being left or careless.
note.cn: 形近组共享 linqu-（留下）家族；近义组是其他被丢下或疏忽的说法。

entries.definition: Shameful failure to do a duty.
To give up or hand over something.
Not doing a duty, or breaking the law.
Left empty and uncared for.
In a state of disrepair.
Not taking proper care.

normalIntro.en: Derelict is de- plus re- plus linqu- leave: left behind completely, whether a building or a duty.
normalIntro.cn: derelict 就是 de- 加 re- 加 linqu-（留下）：被彻底丢下，无论是厂房还是职责。

normal.en: Linqu- means to leave.
normal.cn: linqu- 意为留下。

normal.en: De- and re- together mean completely away.
normal.cn: de- 与 re- 合起来表示彻底丢开。

normal.en: A derelict mill has no workers.
normal.cn: 废弃厂房没有工人。

normal.en: Derelict in duty means neglecting it.
normal.cn: derelict in duty 就是玩忽职守。

normal.en: A derelict on the sand is a left-behind hull.
normal.cn: 沙上的 derelict 是被丢下的船壳。

abstract.en: Half the window glass gone from a mill.
abstract.cn: 一座厂房窗玻璃碎了一半。

abstract.en: An empty square on a duty roster.

abstract.en: A hull sitting on the sand at low tide.

examples.en: The council cleared the derelict site.
examples.cn: 市政清理了那块废弃地。

examples.en: Two derelicts were towed out of the harbour.
examples.cn: 两件遗弃物被拖出港口。

examples.en: He was found derelict in his duty.
examples.cn: 他被认定玩忽职守。

dict_mnemonic.text: derelict 源自拉丁语 derelinquere：de-（彻底）＋ re-（回）＋ linquere（留下）＝彻底丢下不管。丢下的是房子就是「废弃的」，丢下的是职责就是「玩忽职守的」。

root: 拉丁语 linquere（留下）→ relinquere（丢下）→ derelinquere（彻底抛弃）→ derelictus → 英语 derelict

sensesIntro.en: One thing left behind: a mill, a duty and a hull on the sand.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一样被丢下的东西：一座厂房、一份职责与沙上的一具船壳。

core.cn: 核心意象：厂房窗玻璃碎了一半、屋里堆着旧机器，值班表上那一格始终空着

branches.en: Half the window glass gone from a mill.
branches.cn: 一座厂房窗玻璃碎了一半。

branches.en: An empty square on a duty roster.

branches.en: A hull sitting on the sand at low tide.

branches.en: Both are things nobody cares for now.

branches.en: Both result from someone walking away.
branches.cn: 两者都源于有人撒手不管。

intro.en: Derelict is de- plus re- plus linqu-; the leaving root builds the abandoning family.
intro.cn: derelict 由 de- 加 re- 加 linqu- 构成；留下这个词根造出抛弃一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin linquere means to leave, derelinquere to abandon and lapis a stone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linquere 意为留下，derelinquere 意为抛弃，lapis 意为石头。

definition_zh: 派生的；缺乏原创的；衍生物；金融衍生品；（数学）导数
definition_en: derived from something else; lacking originality; or a thing produced from another source
core_image: 一条小溪从大河旁边分出去，水还是那批水，河道却是新的
scene: 实验室里，柳树皮中的化合物被改造成新药：The new drug is a derivative of a compound found in willow bark.
sceneCN: 这里 derivative 是「衍生物」（第 4 个义项：由另一物质经改造而来）；句意：这种新药是柳树皮中一种化合物的衍生物。图中可辨识物件：柳树皮、实验烧瓶、分子结构图、药片。

pos.zh: 派生的；由……衍生的；缺乏原创的
衍生物；衍生品；派生词；导数

collocations.zh: 缺乏原创性的；高度模仿的

senses.title: Coming from another source
senses.definition: formed or developed from something else rather than existing independently
senses.definitionCN: 由他物形成或发展而来，而非独立存在的
senses.example: The design is derivative of an earlier bridge in the same city.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计是从同城一座更早的桥派生出来的。
senses.why: derivare means 'to lead water away from a stream'. A derivative thing is water led off from an existing channel: it flows, but the source is not its own.
senses.whyCN: derivare 意为“从溪流引走水”。derivative 的东西就是从既有水道引出的水：它流动，但源头不属于自己。

senses.title: Lacking originality
senses.titleCN: 缺乏原创的：只是别人的回声
senses.definition: imitative and unoriginal, repeating ideas already used by others
senses.definitionCN: 模仿他人、缺乏原创，重复已有观念
senses.example: Critics called the sequel derivative and predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这部续集缺乏原创、一猜就中。
senses.why: The pejorative sense extends the same image: if everything is led off from another stream, nothing here has its own spring. The word judges the absence of an independent source.
senses.whyCN: 贬义义项是同一意象的延伸：如果一切都从别人的溪流引来，这里就没有自己的泉眼。这个词评判的正是独立源头的缺席。

senses.title: A financial instrument
senses.titleCN: 金融衍生品：价值挂在别的东西上
senses.definition: a financial contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, rate or index
senses.definitionCN: 价值取决于标的资产、利率或指数的金融合约
senses.example: The fund used interest-rate derivatives to hedge its loans.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金用利率衍生品为贷款做对冲。
senses.why: The contract has no independent value; it is led off from a bond, a rate or a price. Finance chose the word because the value literally flows from the underlying.
senses.whyCN: 这种合约没有独立价值，它的价值从债券、利率或价格引出。金融界用这个词，是因为价值确实来自标的。

senses.title: A chemical compound made from another
senses.titleCN: 化学衍生物：改一处就成了新物质
senses.definition: a substance obtained from another by a chemical change, often sharing its core structure
senses.definitionCN: 经化学变化从另一物质得到的物质，通常共享核心结构
senses.example: The derivative is more soluble than the original compound.
senses.exampleCN: 这种衍生物比原化合物更易溶解。
senses.why: Chemists modify one group and keep the skeleton, so the new molecule is a channel led off the old one. The stem is shared; only the branch differs.
senses.whyCN: 化学家改动一个基团、保留骨架，于是新分子就是从旧分子引出的水道。主干共享，只有分支不同。

senses.title: A word formed from another
senses.titleCN: 派生词：从词根长出来的新词
senses.definition: in linguistics, a word formed from an existing word or root by adding affixes or changing its form
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上由既有词或词根加词缀、改变形式而形成的新词
senses.example: The noun 'kindness' is a derivative of the adjective 'kind'.
senses.exampleCN: 名词 kindness 是形容词 kind 的派生词。
senses.why: Word formation is treated as water led from a source: the root supplies the meaning and the suffix opens a new channel, producing a new word.
senses.whyCN: 构词被看成从源头引水：词根提供意义，后缀开出新水道，产生新词。

senses.title: The rate of change in calculus
senses.definition: in mathematics, the rate at which a function changes with respect to one of its variables
senses.definitionCN: 数学中函数相对于某个变量的变化率
senses.example: The derivative of a straight line's position is its constant speed.
senses.exampleCN: 直线运动的位移导数是其恒定速度。
senses.why: A derivative is a value drawn out of a function by a limiting process. The word keeps the sense of something obtained from a larger source, not invented independently.
senses.whyCN: 导数是经极限过程从函数中引出的值。这个词保留了“从更大源头取得而非独立发明”的含义。

senses.title: A work adapted from another
senses.titleCN: 演绎作品：在原作上再创作
senses.definition: in copyright law, a work that adapts or transforms an existing protected work
senses.definitionCN: 版权法中改编或转化既有受保护作品的新作品
senses.example: The film is a derivative work based on a 19th-century novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影是改编自一部 19 世纪小说的演绎作品。
senses.why: Copyright uses the image precisely: the new work draws its substance from the old one, so permission flows with the water.
senses.whyCN: 版权法精确使用了这个意象：新作品从旧作品取得实质内容，因此许可随水一起流动。

senses.title: A secondary product of research
senses.titleCN: 副产品：主流程之外长出来的结果
senses.definition: something produced as a secondary result of a process, project or discovery
senses.definitionCN: 作为某过程、项目或发现的次要结果而产生的东西
senses.example: A useful battery material emerged as a derivative of the space programme.
senses.exampleCN: 一种有用的电池材料作为航天计划的衍生成果出现。
senses.why: Here the source is a process rather than a substance. The result is still led off the main channel, which is why it counts as a derivative rather than a primary product.
senses.whyCN: 这里的源头是过程而不是物质。结果仍从主水道引出，因此算衍生物而不是主产品。

intro.en: Derivative comes from Latin derivare 'to lead water away from a stream', de- 'from' plus rivus 'stream'. English first used it for 'derived things', then for chemistry, linguistics and mathematics; the financial sense is 20th-century.
intro.cn: derivative 来自拉丁 derivare“从溪流引走水”，由 de-“从”和 rivus“溪流”构成。英语最初用它表示“派生之物”，后来用于化学、语言学和数学；金融义是 20 世纪的产物。

items.en: rivus meant 'a small stream or channel'. It also gave English river and rival, the latter from rivalis 'one who uses the same stream'.
items.cn: rivus 意为“小溪、水道”。它也派生了英语 river 和 rival，后者来自 rivalis“共用同一条溪流的人”。

items.en: derivare 'to lead off water' is de- 'from' plus rivare 'to channel'. The literal operation is engineering: a branch canal takes water from a main stream.
items.cn: derivare“引走水”是 de-“从”加 rivare“开渠”。字面操作是工程性的：支渠从主溪流取水。

items.en: Old French deriver passed the verb into English as derive. The adjective and noun derivative followed in the 16th century; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 deriver 把动词以 derive 形式传给英语。形容词与名词 derivative 在 16 世纪跟进，确切最早年代存疑。

items.en: In the 19th century chemistry named a compound made by modifying another as a derivative. The shared skeleton is the main stream, and the change is the branch.
items.cn: 19 世纪化学把经改造另一化合物而得到的物质称为 derivative。共享的骨架是主溪流，改动则是支渠。

items.en: Linguistics applies the term to words formed from roots or other words. A root supplies meaning, and affixes open a new channel.
items.cn: 语言学用该词指由词根或其他词形成的词。词根提供意义，词缀开出新水道。

items.en: Financial derivatives appear in the 20th century. Their value is explicitly derived from an underlying asset, so the metaphor became a definition.
items.cn: 金融衍生品出现于 20 世纪。其价值明确来自标的资产，于是隐喻变成了定义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the derive family and different endings; the near-meaning group separates copied, secondary and mathematically derived things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 derive 词族、词尾不同；近义组区分模仿的、次要的和数学上派生的事物。

entries.definition: to obtain from a source; to originate. It names the act of leading something off, while derivative names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 从某来源获得；起源于。它命名引出动作，而 derivative 命名结果。

entries.definition: the process of deriving, or the origin of a word; the -ation suffix focuses on the process rather than the product.
entries.definitionCN: 推导过程；词源。-ation 后缀聚焦过程而不是产物。

entries.definition: relating to word formation; a derivational affix creates a new word rather than a new grammatical form.
entries.definitionCN: 构词方面的；派生词缀创造新词，而不是新的语法形式。

entries.definition: copying the style or behaviour of others; close to the pejorative sense of derivative, but stresses copying as an act.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿他人风格或行为的；接近 derivative 的贬义，但强调“模仿”这一动作。

entries.definition: coming after or depending on something primary; derivative stresses the source, secondary stresses the rank.
entries.definitionCN: 次要的；在首要事物之后或依赖其存在；derivative 强调来源，secondary 强调等级。

entries.definition: a secondary result of a process; closest to sense 8, but it does not imply that the substance was deliberately derived.
entries.definitionCN: 过程的次要结果；最接近第 8 义，但不暗示该物质是被有意衍生出来的。

entries.definition: a thing that develops from a larger one, like a branch from a stem; it is figurative and less technical than derivative.
entries.definitionCN: 从较大事物发展出来的分支，如同主干上的枝条；它更形象，技术性不如 derivative。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'from' + rivus 'stream': a derivative is water led off from another stream.
normal.cn: de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”：derivative 就是从另一条溪流引出的水。

normal.en: river and rival are cousins from rivus: the rival is the person who shares your stream.
normal.cn: river 和 rival 都是 rivus 的表亲：rival 就是与你共用一条溪流的人。

normal.en: In mathematics, look for the pattern f'(x): the prime mark is the sign that a value has been drawn from the function.
normal.cn: 数学里找 f'(x) 这个写法：撇号就是“从函数中引出值”的标志。

normal.en: The financial phrase is derivative contract; if the value depends on something else, it is a derivative.
normal.cn: 金融搭配是 derivative contract；如果价值取决于别的东西，它就是衍生品。

normal.en: A derivative work in copyright is an adaptation, which is why the same word appears in film and software licences.
normal.cn: 版权中的 derivative work 是改编作品，所以同一个词会出现在电影和软件许可里。

abstract.en: Think of a garden hose split by a Y-connector: the second line carries the same water.
abstract.cn: 想象一根花园水管被 Y 形接头分开：第二条管里流的是同一批水。

abstract.en: Think of a river delta: every channel is the main river redistributed, not a new river.
abstract.cn: 想象一片河口三角洲：每条水道都是主河的重分，而不是一条新河。

abstract.en: Think of a cover song: the melody is borrowed, the performance is new, and both facts matter.
abstract.cn: 想象一首翻唱歌曲：旋律是借来的，演绎是新的，两个事实都重要。

examples.en: Many modern drugs are derivatives of plants used in traditional medicine.
examples.cn: 许多现代药物是传统医学中所用植物的衍生物。

examples.en: The bank lost heavily on derivatives tied to mortgage debt.
examples.cn: 这家银行在与房贷债务挂钩的衍生品上损失惨重。

examples.en: His early paintings are derivative, but the later work has its own voice.
examples.cn: 他早期的画缺乏原创，但后期作品有了自己的声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地river体”——地（de）上的 river（河流）分出一条小水道，就是它的衍生 → derivative 派生的、衍生物

root: 拉丁 derivare“从溪流引水”（de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”）；derivat- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one flow: something is led out of an existing channel, so its existence depends on a source it did not create.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一股水流：某物从既有水道被引出，因此它的存在依赖一个并非自己创造的源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small channel led off from a larger stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：从大河旁引出一条小水道。

branches.en: ORIGINALITY: being led off a stream becomes a judgement when the new channel has no spring of its own.
branches.cn: 原创性：当新水道没有自己的泉眼时，“从别处引水”就变成一种评判。

branches.en: VALUE AND COPYRIGHT: a derivative contract and a derivative work both draw their worth or substance from an underlying original.
branches.cn: 价值与版权：衍生合约与演绎作品都从标的原作取得价值或实质内容。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE AND PROCESS: chemical derivatives and research spin-offs are branches grown from a parent material or project.
branches.cn: 物质与过程：化学衍生物与研究副产品，都是从母体材料或项目长出的分支。

branches.en: WORDS AND NUMBERS: a derived word and a mathematical derivative are both values obtained by a defined operation on a base.
branches.cn: 词与数：派生词与数学导数，都是对基体施加既定运算后得到的值。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: every other sense specifies the kind of source and the kind of channel involved.
branches.cn: 基础义：其余义项都只是说明源头与分支的类型。

intro.en: Derivative is derivat- plus -ive. Latin de- and rivus are fused inside the stem; English productively adds -ive, -ation, -ational and -able to build the family.
intro.cn: derivative 是 derivat- 加 -ive。拉丁 de- 与 rivus 已融合在词干内；英语能产地加 -ive、-ation、-ational、-able 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus 'stream' yields rivulus 'little stream', derivare 'lead off water', and rivalis 'sharing a stream'. English relatives include river, rival, derive and derivation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rivus“溪流”派生 rivulus“小溪”、derivare“引水”、rivalis“共用溪流者”。英语同族词包括 river、rival、derive、derivation。

items.meaning: to obtain from a source; to originate
items.meaningCN: 获得；源自；推导（de-“从”+ rivare“引水”）
items.example: The word derives from an old French term for a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个词源自一个表示边界的古法语词。

items.meaning: the process of deriving; word origin
items.meaningCN: 推导；派生；词源（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The dictionary gives the derivation of the name.
items.exampleCN: 词典给出了这个名字的词源。

items.meaningCN: 派生的；衍生物（-ive 构成形容词与名词）
items.example: The derivative product sold better than the original.
items.exampleCN: 衍生产品比原产品卖得更好。

items.meaning: relating to derivation or word formation
items.meaningCN: 派生的；构词的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The suffix is derivational, not inflectional.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀是派生性的，不是屈折性的。

items.meaning: in a derived or secondary way
items.meaningCN: 派生地；间接地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The right is held derivatively, through the parent company.
items.exampleCN: 这项权利是通过母公司间接持有的。

items.meaningCN: 可推导的；可获得的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The result is derivable from two simple assumptions.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果可以从两个简单假设推导出来。

items.meaning: a large natural stream of water
items.meaningCN: 河流（同源词，rivus 的英语形态）
items.example: The river carries sediment to the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这条河把泥沙带向大海。

items.meaningCN: 竞争对手（同源词，原指共用一条溪流的人）
items.example: The two firms became rivals for the same contract.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司成了同一合同的竞争对手。

definition_zh: 得到；源自；推导出
definition_en: to get something from a source, or to come from a particular origin
core_image: 一条小溪从岩缝里渗出，顺着山势往下越流越宽
scene: 老师带学生沿河往上游走，最后停在山脚一处小小的泉眼边。Many English words derive from Latin roots.
sceneCN: 这里 derive 指「源自」（第 2 个义项：从某个源头而来）；句意是许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。

senses.title: Get something from a source
senses.definition: to get something such as pleasure, income or knowledge from a particular source
senses.definitionCN: 从某一来源获得乐趣、收入或知识等
senses.example: She derives great pleasure from teaching children.
senses.exampleCN: 她从教孩子这件事上得到很大乐趣。
senses.why: The good thing is not made on the spot; it flows in from somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 好处并非当场造出，而是从别处流进来的。

senses.title: Come from an origin
senses.definition: to come from or have its origin in something
senses.definitionCN: 从某事物而来，以其为起源
senses.example: Many English words derive from Latin roots.
senses.exampleCN: 许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。
senses.why: Every stream can be followed back to the spring that fed it.
senses.whyCN: 每条溪流都能顺水追到供它水的那眼泉。

senses.title: Reach by reasoning
senses.definition: to reach a result by reasoning from facts or rules already known
senses.definitionCN: 依据已知事实或规则推理得出结果
senses.example: We can derive the answer from these two simple rules.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以从这两条简单规则推出答案。
senses.why: Reasoning is a channel cut from known ground to a new result.
senses.whyCN: 推理就是从已知的地面开一条渠，通向新的结果。

intro.en: Derive comes from Latin derivare, to lead water away from a stream, built on de- and rivus, a stream, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: derive 来自拉丁语 derivare，本义是把水从河里引走，由 de- 与 rivus（小河）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Rivus named a stream, and derivare meant to lead its water into a new channel.
items.cn: rivus 指小河，derivare 指把河水引进新的渠道。

items.en: Writers extended it from water to words, arguing that one form flows from another.
items.cn: 作家把它从水移到语言上，说一个形式是从另一个形式流出来的。

items.en: French deriver carried the sense of coming from a source.
items.cn: 法语 deriver 带着「自某处而来」的意思。

items.en: English took it up for both obtaining something and tracing an origin.
items.cn: 英语用它同时表示获得某物与追溯来源。

items.en: Science added the mathematical sense of working a result out from rules.
items.cn: 科学又添上从规则算出结果的数学义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -rive sound, while the meaning group runs from starting somewhere to getting and inferring.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -rive 这一段音，近义组则从发源一路走到获得与推断。

entries.definition: to take something away from someone
a form or thing that comes from another
entries.definitionCN: 由另一形式或事物派生的东西

entries.definition: the origin or formation of a word
to begin to exist in a particular place
to get something that you want
to reach a conclusion by reasoning

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with water leaving a spring and end with a rule that yields an answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从水离开泉眼开始，落到一条算出答案的规则。

normal.en: A river and a word both have a spring somewhere upstream.
normal.cn: 河与词，上游都有一眼泉。

normal.en: To derive is to follow the water back, not to invent it.
normal.cn: derive 是顺着水往回找，而不是凭空造水。

normal.en: Pleasure, profit and meaning can all be led into your own field.
normal.cn: 乐趣、收益与意义，都能被引进你自己的田里。

normal.en: The Latin root rivus is a stream, and the word still flows.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基 rivus 是小河，这个词至今还在流。

normal.en: A formula is a channel dug from known facts to a new result.
normal.cn: 公式就是从已知事实挖向新结果的一条渠。

abstract.en: Picture a hand cupping water where it seeps from rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在岩缝渗水处捧起一汪水。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every small tributary points back to one dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每条小支流都指向同一个点。

abstract.en: Picture a proof written line by line until the last line lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一份证明一行行写下去，直到最后一行落定。

examples.en: Many English words derive from Latin roots.
examples.cn: 许多英语单词源自拉丁词根。

examples.en: She derived great pleasure from teaching children.
examples.cn: 她从教孩子这件事上得到很大乐趣。

examples.en: The formula can be derived from two simple rules.
examples.cn: 这个公式可以由两条简单规则推导出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 derive 记成「得瑞武」：de 像「得」，rive 像「河」，从河里得到水，就是获得与源自。

root: 来自拉丁语 derivare，本义是把水从小河里引走，由 de-（离开）与 rivus（小河）组成，经法语 dériver 进入英语。后来从引水引申为获得好处，又引申为追溯来源与推理推导。

sensesIntro.en: From water led out of a stream, to a word traced to its root, to a result reached by rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把水从河里引出，到把一个词追到词根，再到按规则推出结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stream led out of its old channel into a new one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股水被引出旧河道，流进新渠道。

branches.en: The first sense is what the new channel brings you.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是新渠道带给你的东西。

branches.en: The second sense is the spring that every channel starts from.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是每条渠道起步的那眼泉。

branches.en: The third sense is a channel dug by reasoning alone.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是单靠推理挖出的渠道。

branches.en: Getting and coming from are the two ends of one flow.
branches.cn: 获得与源自，是同一条水流的上下游两端。

branches.en: A word traced to its root and a result traced to its rules use the same backward walk.
branches.cn: 词追到词根、结果追到规则，用的是同一种往回走的步子。

intro.en: Derive has a small Latin family built on a stream and on the act of leading water away.
intro.cn: derive 有一小族拉丁词，建在「小河」与「引水」这两件事上。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin rivus, a stream, and de- adds the sense of away or down.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 rivus（小河），前缀 de- 添上离开、向下的意思。

items.meaning: to lead or draw from a source
items.example: They derive support from old friends.
items.exampleCN: 他们从老朋友那里得到支持。

items.meaning: the act of tracing an origin
items.example: The derivation of the word is unclear.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的来历并不清楚。

items.example: Credit is a derivative of that Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: credit 是那个拉丁动词的派生词。

items.example: The result is derivable from the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果可以从数据推出。

items.example: The drug is derived from a common plant.
items.exampleCN: 这种药是从一种常见植物中提取的。

items.meaning: the act of getting from a source
items.example: He is deriving a new model.
items.exampleCN: 他正在推导一个新模型。

items.meaning: in a way that comes from something else

definition_zh: v. 除去…的盐分；淡化（海水）
definition_en: to remove salt from sea water so that it can be used
core_image: 海边厂房里一排反渗透膜，海水进去，淡水出来，浓盐水另走一根管
scene: 这座厂为镇上淡化海水。The plant desalinises sea water for the town.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：desalinises 指淡化；句意是这座厂为镇上淡化海水。

senses.title: Remove salt from water
senses.definition: to take the salt out of sea water so it can be drunk or used
senses.definitionCN: 把海水里的盐去掉，使其可饮用或使用
senses.example: The plant desalinises sea water for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座厂为镇上淡化海水。
senses.why: A row of membranes with fresh water on one side.
senses.whyCN: 一排膜，一侧流出淡水。

senses.title: Treat soil or produce
senses.definition: to remove excess salt from soil or from a food product
senses.definitionCN: 去掉土壤或食品中过多的盐分
senses.example: They desalinise the soil before planting.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在种植前先给土壤脱盐。
senses.why: A field flushed with fresh water after harvest.
senses.whyCN: 一块收获后用清水冲洗过的田。

senses.title: Supply a dry region
senses.definition: to provide a dry region with usable water by this method
senses.definitionCN: 用这种方法为干旱地区提供可用水
senses.example: The city desalinises to survive the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市靠淡化来熬过干旱。
senses.why: A coastal pipe feeding an inland reservoir.
senses.whyCN: 一根海岸管道向内陆修水池供水。

intro.en: Desalinise is de-, removal, plus saline, from Latin sal, salt, plus the verb suffix -ise.
intro.cn: desalinise 由 de-（去掉）加 saline（含盐的）加动词后缀 -ise 构成，saline 源自拉丁语 sal（盐）。

items.en: Sal meant salt.
items.cn: sal 意为盐。

items.en: Salinus meant of salt.
items.cn: salinus 意为盐的。

items.en: Saline entered English for salty water.
items.cn: 十九世纪 saline 指盐水。

items.en: Desalinise was formed for removing that salt.
items.cn: 二十世纪 desalinise 被造出来表示去掉这些盐。

items.en: Reverse osmosis made it an industry term.
items.cn: 反渗透让它成为工业术语。

items.en: Dry coastal states use it in policy papers.
items.cn: 干旱的沿海国家在政策文件中使用它。

note.cn: 形近组共享 sal-（盐）家族；近义组是其他把水弄干净的说法。

normalIntro.cn: desalinise 就是 de-（去掉）加 sal-（盐）加 -ise：让盐离开。

normal.en: Sal- means salt, as in saline.
normal.cn: sal- 意为盐，如 saline。

normal.en: De- means removal.
normal.cn: de- 表示去掉。

normal.en: -ise makes it a verb.
normal.cn: -ise 把它变成动词。

normal.en: Desalinise sea water and it can be drunk.
normal.cn: 淡化海水后就能饮用。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一次去盐：一排膜、一块田与一根海岸管道。

branches.cn: 两者都把海水变成可用水源。

definition_zh: 下降；传下来；突然降临
definition_en: to move from a higher place to a lower one, or to come down through time
core_image: 石阶一级级往下，尽头没入山谷里的白雾
scene: 山路上天色转暗，石阶湿滑，大家扶着栏杆一步步往下走。The path descends steeply toward the river.
sceneCN: 这里 descend 指「下降」（第 1 个义项：从高处往低处走）；句意是小路陡峭地向河边下降。

senses.title: Move to a lower place
senses.definition: to go down from a higher place to a lower one
senses.definitionCN: 从较高的地方走到较低的地方
senses.example: The plane began to descend through the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机开始穿过云层下降。
senses.why: Gravity offers the easy direction; the body only has to allow it.
senses.whyCN: 重力早已备好省力的方向，身体只需允许它发生。

senses.title: Be passed down
senses.definition: to be handed down from an earlier time or from earlier people
senses.definitionCN: 从更早的年代或更早的人那里传下来
senses.example: The custom has descended from medieval times.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗从中世纪传下来。
senses.why: What comes down a family line arrives the way water comes down a hill.
senses.whyCN: 沿血脉传下来的东西，抵达的方式就像水往山下流。

senses.title: Arrive suddenly in numbers
senses.definition: to arrive suddenly and in large numbers, often in a troubling way
senses.definitionCN: 大批地突然到来，常带有令人不安的意味
senses.example: Reporters descended on the small village overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 记者一夜之间涌进这个小村庄。
senses.why: A crowd can fall on a place the way weather falls on it.
senses.whyCN: 人群扑向一个地方，就像天气压下来一样。

intro.en: Descend goes back to Latin descendere, built from de-, down, and scandere, to climb, and it crossed through Old French into English.
intro.cn: descend 可追到拉丁语 descendere，由 de-（向下）与 scandere（攀爬）构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Scandere meant to climb, so descendere meant to climb down.
items.cn: scandere 指攀爬，因此 descendere 指往下爬。

items.en: The image was always bodily: a foot finding a lower step.
items.cn: 这个意象一直是身体性的：一只脚找到更低的一级台阶。

items.en: Descendre kept both the downward motion and the sense of lineage.
items.cn: descendre 同时保留了向下移动与血统这两层意思。

items.en: English used it for stairs, rivers and family lines alike.
items.cn: 英语把它同样用于台阶、河流与家族世系。

items.en: It now also describes crowds and troubles that arrive all at once.
items.cn: 如今它也形容一下子涌来的大批人与麻烦。

note.en: The look-alike group all carry the -scend or -scent shape, and the meaning group all describe a downward movement.
note.cn: 形近组都带着 -scend 或 -scent 的形状，近义组则都表示向下移动。

entries.definition: the act of going down, or a family line
a person who comes from an earlier family
to behave as if you are above others
entries.definitionCN: 表现得好像高别人一等

entries.definition: to move downward without control
to move quickly to a lower position
to go down slowly below a surface
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢沉到某个表面以下

normalIntro.en: These hooks start on a wet stone stair and end with a crowd pouring into a quiet street.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一级湿滑的石阶开始，落到涌进安静街道的人群。

normal.en: Every stair is a small promise that the ground will rise to meet you.
normal.cn: 每一级台阶都在悄悄保证：地面会升上来接住你。

normal.en: The same word carries a body down and a family name forward.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既把身体送下去，也把姓氏传下去。

normal.en: A crowd descends the way rain does: all at once, from above.
normal.cn: 人群的到来像雨：从上方一下子落下来。

normal.en: Climb up and you ascend; climb down and you descend.
normal.cn: 往上爬是 ascend，往下爬就是 descend。

normal.en: A descendant is simply someone who came down the family stairs.
normal.cn: 后裔不过是从家族那道楼梯走下来的人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding along a cold stone rail.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手沿着冰冷的石栏滑下去。

abstract.en: Picture a valley filling with mist as the path goes lower.
abstract.cn: 想象路越走越低，雾气渐渐填满山谷。

abstract.en: Picture thirty reporters standing at one narrow door.
abstract.cn: 想象三十名记者挤在一扇窄门前。

root: 来自拉丁语 descendere，由 de-（向下）与 scandere（攀爬）组成，经古法语 descendre 进入英语。本义是沿台阶往下走，后来用于血统的传承，也形容人或麻烦大批突然到来。

sensesIntro.en: From a foot taking a lower step, to a family line handed down, to a crowd falling on a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只脚踩向更低一级台阶，到一条传下来的血脉，再到扑向某处的人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot finding the next step down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚去找下一级向下的台阶。

branches.en: The first sense is plain downward motion.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是单纯的向下移动。

branches.en: The second sense sends the same motion through time instead of space.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同一种移动从空间移到了时间上。

branches.en: The third sense is motion that arrives all at once, like weather.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一下子到来的移动，像天气那样。

branches.en: Stairs and generations share one picture: each step passes something down.
branches.cn: 台阶与世代共用一幅图：每一级都把东西传下去。

branches.en: A plane and a crowd both leave the height they were at.
branches.cn: 飞机与人群都离开了原来所在的高处。

intro.en: Descend builds a family around going down, family lines and the idea of stepping lower.
intro.cn: descend 长出一族词，围绕向下、血统以及「踏低一级」这个动作。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is scandere, to climb, and de- turns the climb downward.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 scandere（攀爬），前缀 de- 把这次攀爬转向下方。

items.exampleCN: 他们的后代仍住在这里。

items.exampleCN: 把名字按从大到小的顺序排列。

definition_zh: 后代；后裔；（物种、语言等的）衍生者；由早先事物发展而来的产物
definition_en: a person, animal or thing that comes from an earlier ancestor, species or source
core_image: 一条向下的石阶从祖辈的门口铺到孙辈的脚下，每一级都稳稳踩在前一级上
scene: 族谱摊在长桌上，最末一页写着一个刚出生的名字，The archivist points to the youngest descendant in the register.
sceneCN: 这里 descendant 指「由祖先一脉相传下来的后人」（第 1 个义项：直系血统上的后代）；句意为档案员指着族谱里最年幼的那位后代。图中可辨识物件：摊开的族谱、长桌、指页的手指、墨迹未干的名字。

derivatives.zh: 屈尊；带着优越感地俯就

senses.title: A person born of an ancestor
senses.definition: a person who is descended from a particular ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 从某位祖先一脉传下来的人
senses.example: Every descendant of the founder received a copy of the will.
senses.exampleCN: 创始人的每一位后代都拿到了一份遗嘱副本。
senses.why: descendant is the present participle of descend, so the person is literally one who is going down the family line from the ancestor.
senses.whyCN: descendant 是 descend 的现在分词，字面就是「沿着家族这条线从祖先往下走的人」。

senses.title: The later members of a line, taken together
senses.definition: all the later members of a family regarded as one body
senses.definitionCN: 把某一家族后来各代的人合起来看
senses.example: The estate is now run by his descendants as a working farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这座庄园现在由他的后人当作农场经营。
senses.why: the singular form can name a group because a line of descent is thought of as one stream rather than separate persons.
senses.whyCN: 单数形式能指一群人，因为「一脉」在说话人心里是一股水流，而不是一个个孤立的人。

senses.title: A species derived from an earlier one
senses.titleCN: 由早期物种演化而来的物种
senses.definition: an organism that has evolved from an earlier species
senses.definitionCN: 由更早的物种演化出来的生物
senses.example: Modern maize is a descendant of a wild grass from southern Mexico.
senses.exampleCN: 现代玉米是墨西哥南部一种野草的衍生种。
senses.why: the family metaphor carries over to evolution: a species stands in the same relation to its ancestor as a child to a parent.
senses.whyCN: 家族的比喻被搬到演化上：一个物种与其祖先的关系，正如孩子与父母的关系。

senses.title: A language derived from another
senses.titleCN: 由另一语言分化出的语言
senses.definition: a language that developed from an earlier parent language
senses.definitionCN: 由更早的母语分化发展出来的语言
senses.example: French, Spanish and Italian are descendants of Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 法语、西班牙语和意大利语都是拉丁语的衍生语言。
senses.why: linguists borrowed the genealogy image directly, so a daughter language is called a descendant rather than an offshoot.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家直接借用了谱系意象，因此子语言被称作 descendant，而不是旁枝。

senses.title: A thing copied or developed from an earlier form
senses.titleCN: 由先前形态发展或复制而来的事物
senses.definition: an object or version that has been developed from an earlier one
senses.definitionCN: 由更早的物件或版本发展出来的东西
senses.example: This compact model is a descendant of the first field radio.
senses.exampleCN: 这款轻便机型是最早的野战电台的后继型号。
senses.why: when a design is changed step by step, each stage looks like a child of the one before, so the word spreads from people to products.
senses.whyCN: 设计一步步改动时，每一阶段都像前一阶段的子代，于是这个词从人扩展到产品。

senses.title: A legal heir in the direct line
senses.definition: in law, a person entitled to inherit because of direct descent
senses.definitionCN: 法律上因直系血缘而有继承资格的人
senses.example: The court ruled that the nephew was not a descendant under the statute.
senses.exampleCN: 法院裁定，这位侄子在该法条下不属于直系后代。
senses.why: inheritance law needs an exact word for the direct line, so the everyday family sense is narrowed into a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 继承法需要给直系这条线一个精确的词，于是日常的家族义被收窄为法律类别。

senses.title: Going downward in direction
senses.definition: moving or sloping downward, as in the rare adjective use
senses.definitionCN: 向下移动或向下倾斜的（罕用形容词义）
senses.example: A descendant branch of the river drops toward the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 河道一条向下的支流朝沼泽落去。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the oldest physical sense of de- plus scandere, climbing down, which the noun use later overshadowed.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了 de- 加 scandere「向下爬」这层最古老的物理义，后来被名词用法盖过。

senses.title: A later result of an event or idea
senses.titleCN: 事件或想法在后世结出的结果
senses.definition: something that follows from and is shaped by an earlier event or idea
senses.definitionCN: 由更早的事件或观念引出并受其塑造的事物
senses.example: The current subsidy scheme is a descendant of wartime rationing.
senses.exampleCN: 现行的补贴方案是战时配给制的后续产物。
senses.why: the idea of inheritance is loosened until anything shaped by an earlier thing can be called its descendant.
senses.whyCN: 「继承」的观念被放宽，凡是受早先事物塑造的东西，都可称作它的后代。

intro.en: Descendant is the English present participle of descend, built on Latin scandere 'to climb' with the prefix de- 'down'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: descendant 是 descend 的英语现在分词形式，底层是拉丁 scandere「攀登」加前缀 de-「向下」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Scandere meant 'to climb'. Its deeper pre-Latin base is a reconstructed form, and the usual suggestion of a root meaning 'to leap' is a hypothesis rather than an attested fact.
items.cn: scandere 意为「攀登」。它在拉丁语之前的词基属重构形式；通常把它联系到一个意为「跳」的词根，这只是假说，并非有书证的事实。

items.en: De- 'down' plus scandere gave descendere 'to climb down, go down'. Classical Latin already used it for coming down from a stock or source.
items.cn: de-「向下」加 scandere 构成 descendere「爬下来、下去」。古典拉丁语已用它表示「出自某一血统或来源」。

items.en: The present participle descendens, genitive descendentis, meant 'going down' and also 'deriving from'.
items.cn: 现在分词 descendens（属格 descendentis）意为「向下的」，也有「源自」的意思。

items.en: Old French took the participle as descendant and used it of a person who comes from a stock.
items.cn: 古法语把这个分词写作 descendant，用来指由某一血统传下来的人。

items.en: English adopted descendant in the fourteenth century, first as an adjective and then as a noun for the person.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪引入 descendant，先作形容词，后作指人的名词。

items.en: Descendent also appears, modelled on the Latin stem; source uncertain which spelling entered English first, and descendant is now the standard form.
items.cn: 也见 descendent 这一拼法，是照着拉丁词干造的；两种拼法孰先进入英语来源不确定，现在以 descendant 为标准。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same Latin verb that are easily confused in spelling; the second holds words for later family members that do not share the root.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个拉丁动词的各形态，拼写极易混淆；第二组指同样表示后人的词，但词根不同。

entries.definition: An alternative spelling of the same word, shaped on the Latin stem; it is not a separate meaning and is now less standard.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的另一种拼法，照着拉丁词干写成；并非另一个词义，如今较不规范。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to go down or to come from an ancestor; the noun names the person, the verb names the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为下降或传自某祖先；名词指人，动词指动作。

entries.definition: The act of going down, a downward slope, or the fact of being related by blood; it never names the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指下降的动作、下坡，或血缘关系这一事实；从不指人。

entries.definition: To lower oneself to deal with inferiors; the downward image survives as social slumming rather than family descent.
entries.definitionCN: 屈尊与地位低的人打交道；向下的意象保留为社会意义上的俯就，而非家族传承。

entries.definition: A child or the young of an animal, usually the direct product of a parent rather than a remote generation.
entries.definitionCN: 子女或动物的幼仔，通常指父母的直接产物，而非隔了很多代的后人。

entries.definition: Descendants considered as a group, often with a tone of lineage or stock; more formal than descendant.
entries.definitionCN: 把后代作为一个群体来看，常带血统或族系的意味；比 descendant 正式。

entries.definition: A person who receives property or a title; descent is one route to being an heir, but inheritance is the point.
entries.definitionCN: 接受财产或头衔的人；血缘是成为继承人的一条途径，但重点在继承。

entries.definition: The person from whom one is descended; the mirror image of descendant on the same family line.
entries.definitionCN: 自己由之传下来的人；是同一条家族线上 descendant 的镜像。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real family of words and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: de- 'down' + scandere 'climb' = one who climbs down the family tree from the ancestor.
normal.cn: de-「向下」+ scandere「爬」= 沿家族树从祖先往下爬的人。

normal.en: The same verb gives descend, descent, condescend, ascend and transcend.
normal.cn: 同一个动词还给出 descend、descent、condescend、ascend、transcend。

normal.en: -ant marks the person, as in applicant, attendant and occupant.
normal.cn: -ant 标记「人」，如 applicant、attendant、occupant。

normal.en: The word usually follows direct, lineal or remote, which grade how far back the line runs.
normal.cn: 这个词常跟在 direct、lineal、remote 之后，用来说明这条线往上追得多远。

normal.en: In biology and linguistics it pairs with ancestor as the standard term for a derived form.
normal.cn: 在生物学与语言学里，它与 ancestor 配对，是表示「衍生形态」的标准词。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where each step carries a name carved by the step above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一架楼梯，每一级都刻着由上一级刻下的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a river that splits again and again, yet every channel still carries the same water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条不断分岔的河，每一道支流里流的仍是同一股水。

abstract.en: Picture a seed packet labelled with the name of the garden it came from.
abstract.cn: 想象一只种子袋，标签上写着它来自的那座园子。

examples.en: She is a direct descendant of the family that built the mill.
examples.cn: 她是建造这座磨坊的家族的直系后代。

examples.en: The languages of the region are all descendants of one older tongue.
examples.cn: 这一地区的语言都是同一种更古老语言的衍生语言。

examples.en: Today's lightweight laptop is a descendant of machines that filled a whole room.
examples.cn: 今天的轻薄笔记本是那些占满整间屋子的机器的后代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得森登特」听成「得孙等它」——祖先往下等，等到孙子这一代，就是后代。de 向下，scend 爬，向下爬出来的就是后人。

root: 拉丁 scandere「攀登」加 de-「向下」构成 descendere「爬下来、下来」，其现在分词 descendens 经古法语 descendant 进入英语。scandere 在拉丁语之前的词基属重构形式，通常联系的「跳」义只是假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one downward line: first the person, then the group, then the derived species, language and object, then the legal heir, the rare downward adjective and finally any later result.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条向下的线展开：先是人，再是一群人，再是衍生的物种、语言与物件，然后是法定继承人、罕用的「向下」形容词，最后是任何后世结出的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase running down from an ancestor's door to a child's feet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架从祖先门口向下铺到孩子脚下的楼梯。

branches.en: ONE PERSON AND THE WHOLE LINE: the same word names a single heir and the group of later members, because both sit below the ancestor.
branches.cn: 一个人与整条线：同一个词既指单个后人，也指后来全体成员，因为两者都位于祖先之下。

branches.en: SPECIES AND LANGUAGE: evolution and linguistics both reuse the family tree, so a new species or a daughter language is a descendant.
branches.cn: 物种与语言：演化与语言学都借用了家族树，因此新物种或子语言都叫 descendant。

branches.en: DERIVED OBJECT: a revised design inherits features from its earlier model the way a child inherits traits.
branches.cn: 衍生物件：改过的设计从旧型号继承特征，正如孩子继承父母的性状。

branches.en: LEGAL HEIR: the direct line is narrowed into a person with a right to inherit.
branches.cn: 法定继承人：直系这条线被收窄为有继承权的人。

branches.en: DOWNWARD AND AFTERWARD: the physical sense of going down survives in the adjective, while the temporal sense of coming after survives in the figurative result.
branches.cn: 向下与在后：向下的物理义留在形容词里，而「在其后」的时间义留在比喻性的结果里。

intro.en: Descendant can be read from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb stem and an English participial ending.
intro.cn: descendant 可以按拉丁前缀、拉丁动词词干与英语分词词尾逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandere supplies the climbing image to descend, descent, ascend, transcend and the ladder word scale, while de- fixes the direction as downward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 scandere 为 descend、descent、ascend、transcend 以及表示梯子的 scale 提供「攀爬」意象，de- 则把方向定为向下。

items.example: The prefix turns climbing into climbing down.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「往上爬」变成「往下爬」。

items.example: The stem supplies the upward motion that de- reverses.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供向上的动作，再由 de- 反转。

items.meaningCN: 正在做或处于某状态的人或物
items.example: The ending also marks applicant and occupant.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾也见于 applicant 与 occupant。

items.meaning: to go down; to come from a stock
items.example: The path descends to the river.
The descent from the ridge took two hours.
items.exampleCN: 从山脊下撤用了两个小时。

items.example: He condescended to explain the rule.
items.exampleCN: 他屈尊解释了这条规则。

items.example: The map is drawn to a scale of one to fifty thousand.
items.exampleCN: 这幅地图按五万分之一的比例尺绘制。

latinEntries.meaning: to climb down; to be derived from

derivatives.meaning: the later members of a line
having come down or come from a stock

definition_zh: n. 下降；下坡；血统；世系；（突然）袭击
definition_en: an act of going down, a family origin, or a sudden attack
core_image: 登山者沿陡坡一步步往下，家谱树一层层往下分叉，族谱上写着祖籍
scene: 下山用了两个小时。The descent took two hours.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：descent 指下降；句意是下山用了两个小时。

pos.zh: 下降；下坡；血统；世系；（突然）袭击

senses.title: Going down
senses.definition: the act of moving from a higher to a lower place
senses.definitionCN: 从高处移到低处的行为
senses.example: The descent took two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 下山用了两个小时。
senses.why: A climber stepping down a steep slope.
senses.whyCN: 一个沿陡坡一步步往下的登山者。

senses.title: A downward slope
senses.definition: a slope or path that goes down
senses.definitionCN: 往下走的坡或路
senses.example: The road makes a sharp descent to the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路陡降到海湾。
senses.why: A road dropping in switchbacks to the water.
senses.whyCN: 一条以之字形落到水边的路。

senses.title: Family origin
senses.definition: the family or country that a person comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所来自的家族或国家
senses.example: She is of Irish descent.
senses.exampleCN: 她是爱尔兰裔。
senses.why: A family tree branching downwards on paper.
senses.whyCN: 纸上一棵往下分叉的家谱树。

senses.title: A sudden attack
senses.definition: a sudden visit or attack by a group
senses.definitionCN: 一群人突然的到访或袭击
senses.example: The police made a descent on the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 警方突袭了那座仓库。
senses.why: Boats landing on a beach before dawn.
senses.whyCN: 天亮前抢滩登陆的船。

intro.en: Descent comes from Latin descensus, from descendere, de- plus scandere, to climb: a climbing down.
intro.cn: descent 源自拉丁语 descensus，来自 descendere，由 de- 加 scandere（攀登）构成：往下爬。

items.en: Scandere meant to climb.
items.cn: scandere 意为攀登。

items.en: Descendere meant to climb down.
items.cn: descendere 意为往下爬。

items.en: Descensus named the act of going down.
items.cn: descensus 指下降这一行为。

items.en: Descent entered English for going down.
items.cn: 十三世纪 descent 以下降义进入英语。

items.en: It came to name family lineage.
items.cn: 十四世纪转而指家族世系。

items.en: It also named a sudden landing or attack.
items.cn: 十七世纪也指突然登陆或袭击。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scend- climbing family; the near-meaning group names other downward things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 scend-（攀登）家族；近义组是其他「往下」的说法。

entries.definition: To move from a higher to a lower place.
A person descended from an ancestor.
The act of going up.
A fall to a lower level.
The line of ancestors a person comes from.
A sudden attack on a place.

normalIntro.en: Descent is de- down plus scend- climb: a climbing down, whether a slope, a family tree or an attack.
normalIntro.cn: descent 就是 de-（向下）加 scend-（攀登）：往下爬，无论是坡、家谱还是袭击。

normal.en: Scend- means to climb, as in ascend.
normal.cn: scend- 意为攀登，如 ascend。

normal.en: De- means down.
normal.cn: de- 表示向下。

normal.en: The descent took two hours.
normal.cn: 下山用了两个小时。

normal.en: Of Irish descent means Irish ancestry.
normal.cn: of Irish descent 指爱尔兰血统。

normal.en: A descent on a place is a sudden raid.
normal.cn: a descent on a place 指突然袭击。

abstract.en: A climber stepping down a steep slope.
abstract.cn: 一个沿陡坡一步步往下的登山者。

abstract.en: A road dropping in switchbacks to the water.
abstract.cn: 一条以之字形落到水边的路。

abstract.en: A family tree branching downwards on paper.
abstract.cn: 纸上一棵往下分叉的家谱树。

examples.en: The plane began its descent at noon.
examples.cn: 飞机中午开始下降。

examples.en: Two descents were logged by the rescue team.
examples.cn: 救援队记录了两次下撤。

examples.en: His family is of Italian descent.
examples.cn: 他家是意大利裔。

dict_mnemonic.text: descent 源自拉丁语 descendere：de-（向下）＋ scandere（攀登）＝往下爬。名词 descent 既指「下降、下坡」，也指家谱往下传的「血统」，还指突然扑下来的「突袭」。

root: 拉丁语 scandere（攀登）→ de-＋scandere → descendere（往下爬）→ descensus → 英语 descent

sensesIntro.en: One going down: a slope, a family tree and a landing at dawn.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次往下：一段坡、一棵家谱树与一次天亮前的登陆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a climber stepping down a steep slope while a family tree branches downwards on paper
core.cn: 核心意象：登山者沿陡坡一步步往下，纸上的家谱树一层层往下分叉

branches.en: A climber stepping down a steep slope.
branches.cn: 一个沿陡坡一步步往下的登山者。

branches.en: A road dropping in switchbacks to the water.

branches.en: A family tree branching downwards on paper.

branches.en: Boats landing on a beach before dawn.
branches.cn: 天亮前抢滩登陆的船。

branches.en: Both move from high ground to low.
branches.cn: 两者都从高处移到低处。

intro.en: Descent is de- plus scend-; the climbing root builds the up-and-down family.
intro.cn: descent 由 de- 加 scend- 构成；攀登这个词根造出上下两族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandere means to climb, descendere to climb down and gradus a step.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandere 意为攀登，descendere 意为往下爬，gradus 意为步。

definition_zh: 描述；形容；把……称作
definition_en: to say what someone or something is like
core_image: 一个人用手指在空气里勾出轮廓，让旁人看见他脑中的形状
scene: 目击者在警局里回忆那个人的样子，从身高一直说到外套的颜色。She described the man carefully to the police.
sceneCN: 这里 describe 指「描述」（第 1 个义项：用语言说出某人某物的样子）；句意是她向警方仔细描述了那个人。

senses.title: Say what something is like
senses.definition: to say what someone or something is like by giving details
senses.definitionCN: 通过给出细节说出某人某物的样子
senses.example: She described the man carefully to the police.
senses.exampleCN: 她向警方仔细描述了那个人。
senses.why: The speaker lends his eyes to a listener who was not there.
senses.whyCN: 说的人把自己的眼睛借给一个不在场的听者。

senses.title: Call it by a name
senses.definition: to say that something is of a certain kind or quality
senses.definitionCN: 说某事物属于某种类型或具有某种性质
senses.example: He described the plan as a waste of money.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这个计划称作浪费钱。
senses.why: Once you have traced the shape, you can pin a label on it.
senses.whyCN: 轮廓描完之后，就可以在上面别一个标签。

senses.title: Trace a shape through space
senses.definition: to move along a path so that it forms a particular shape
senses.definitionCN: 沿某条路线移动，从而形成一个特定形状
senses.example: The needle described a clean arc on the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 指针在纸上画出一道干净的弧线。
senses.why: A moving thing can write its own outline without a hand.
senses.whyCN: 会动的东西不必用手，也能写下自己的轮廓。

intro.en: Describe comes straight from Latin describere, built on de-, down, and scribere, to write, so its oldest picture is an outline written down.
intro.cn: describe 直接来自拉丁语 describere，由 de-（向下）与 scribere（写）构成，最古老的画面就是被写下来的轮廓。

items.en: Scribere meant to write or scratch marks, and describere meant to copy out a shape.
items.cn: scribere 指书写或刻痕，describere 指把一个形状照样描下来。

items.en: Surveyors used it for marking out land on a map.
items.cn: 测量员用它来表示在地图上标出一块土地。

items.en: English borrowed it for setting down a scene in words.
items.cn: 英语借它来表示用文字把一个场景记下来。

items.en: It gained the weaker sense of calling something by a name.
items.cn: 它又添了一层较弱的用法：给某物安上一个名号。

items.en: Science kept the old geometric sense of a path traced in space.
items.cn: 科学保留了它古老的几何义：在空间里划出的一条路径。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scribe element, while the meaning group all put a scene into words or pictures.
note.cn: 形近组共用 scribe 这一段，近义组则都把场景变成文字或画面。

entries.definition: words that tell what something is like
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物是什么样子的文字

entries.definition: to order a medicine or a rule
to pay to receive something regularly
to show something in a picture or in words
entries.definitionCN: 用图画或文字表现某物

entries.definition: to represent a person or scene in art
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术中表现人物或场景

entries.definition: to make something clear to someone
entries.definitionCN: 使某事物对人变得清楚

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a finger drawing a shape in the air and end with a label pinned on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一根手指在空中画出形状开始，落到别在上面的一个标签。

normal.en: A description is a picture made of words instead of lines.
normal.cn: 一段描述就是用词而不是线条画出的图。

normal.en: If a listener can draw it, the describing worked.
normal.cn: 如果听的人能画出来，这段描述就成功了。

normal.en: De- plus scribere is writing something down from top to bottom.
normal.cn: de- 加 scribere，就是把东西从上到下写下来。

normal.en: To describe a plan as foolish is to hand it a label.
normal.cn: 把一个计划说成愚蠢，就是给它贴上一张标签。

normal.en: A needle can describe an arc with no hand at all.
normal.cn: 一根指针不用手，也能画出一道弧。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing a face in the empty air.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在空里描出一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a list so exact that two strangers pick the same coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一份清单精确到两个陌生人会挑中同一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a museum label that is longer than the object.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比展品本身还长的博物馆标签。

examples.en: She described the man carefully to the police.
examples.cn: 她向警方仔细描述了那个人。

examples.en: The report describes how the money was spent.
examples.cn: 这份报告说明了钱是怎么花掉的。

examples.en: He described the plan as a waste of money.
examples.cn: 他把这个计划称作浪费钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 describe 记成「地斯快布」：de 向下，scribe 是写，把眼前的样子一笔笔写下来，就是描述。

root: 来自拉丁语 describere，由 de-（向下）与 scribere（写）组成。本义是一笔一笔写下来、描出轮廓，后来引申为用语言叙述与形容，也可表示把某物称作什么。

sensesIntro.en: From an outline written down, to a name attached to it, to a path traced by a moving thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被写下来的轮廓，到贴在轮廓上的名字，再到移动之物划出的轨迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tracing an outline that others cannot see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手描出别人看不见的轮廓。

chain: AN EYE TAKES IN A SHAPE

branches.en: The first sense is the outline handed over in words.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是用语言交出去的轮廓。

branches.en: The second sense is the label fixed at the end of the tracing.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是描完之后别上去的标签。

branches.en: The third sense lets the outline draw itself by moving.
branches.cn: 第三个义项让轮廓靠移动把自己画出来。

branches.en: Telling what a thing is like often ends in naming what it is.
branches.cn: 说清一个东西的样子，常常以说出它是什么收尾。

branches.en: Both senses leave a visible line behind, one in words, one in space.
branches.cn: 两个义项都留下看得见的线，一个在文字里，一个在空间里。

intro.en: Describe gathers words about writing an outline down, from a short account to something beyond words.
intro.cn: describe 聚起一族词，都与写下轮廓有关，从简短的叙述到无法用言语形容。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is scribere, to write, and de- adds the sense of writing something down in full.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 scribere（写），前缀 de- 添上「完整写下来」的意思。

items.exampleCN: 把那个房间描述给我听。
这个描述与那个窃贼相符。
这是一个描述性的标题。
这个词是以描述方式使用的。

items.meaning: able to be put into words
items.exampleCN: 这种感觉几乎无法描述。

items.meaning: a word or sign that labels
items.example: Add a descriptor to each file.
items.exampleCN: 给每个文件加一个标识词。
这则广告错误地描述了那套房子。

definition_zh: 沙漠；荒原；抛弃
definition_en: a large dry area of land with little rain, or to leave someone and never return
core_image: 一片望不到边的沙丘，风把沙脊一条条往前推
scene: 正午的太阳把沙丘照得发白，向导说再走半天也见不到水。Few plants can survive in the desert.
sceneCN: 这里 desert 指「沙漠」（第 1 个义项：干旱少雨的大片沙地）；句意是很少植物能在沙漠里存活。

senses.title: A dry sea of sand
senses.definition: a large area of dry land where almost nothing grows because there is very little rain
senses.definitionCN: 因降雨极少而几乎长不出东西的大片干地
senses.example: Few plants can survive in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 很少植物能在沙漠里存活。
senses.why: Land becomes desert when water stops arriving faster than it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 当水离开的速度一直快过到来的速度，土地就成了沙漠。

senses.title: Leave someone behind
senses.definition: to leave a person or place and never come back
senses.definitionCN: 离开某人或某地且再也不回来
senses.example: He deserted his family and moved to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 他抛弃了家人，搬到另一座城市。
senses.why: To desert is to make a place or a person into empty land.
senses.whyCN: 抛弃，就是把一个人或一个地方变成空掉的荒地。

senses.title: Leave a duty behind
senses.definition: to leave military service or a post without permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许离开军队或岗位
senses.example: The soldier deserted from the army in his second year.
senses.exampleCN: 那名士兵在第二年逃离了军队。
senses.why: The abandoned post is as empty as the abandoned plain.
senses.whyCN: 被丢下的岗位，和那片被丢下的荒原一样空。

intro.en: Desert comes from Latin desertum, something left empty, from deserere, to abandon, built on de- and serere, to join.
intro.cn: desert 来自拉丁语 desertum，意为被丢空的地方，源于 deserere（舍弃），由 de- 与 serere（连接）构成。

items.en: Deserere meant to undo a bond, to leave a thing unjoined and alone.
items.cn: deserere 指把一条联结解开，让某物孤立无依。

items.en: Desertum named any place left empty, not only sand.
items.cn: desertum 指任何被丢空的地方，并不只指沙地。

items.en: French desert carried both the empty land and the act of abandoning.
items.cn: 法语 desert 同时带着空地和舍弃这两个意思。

items.en: English split the two uses between a noun of sand and a verb of leaving.
items.cn: 英语把两种用法分开：名词指沙地，动词指离开。

items.en: Dryness became the main sense, and the verb kept the human one.

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a ridge of sand and end with an empty chair at a table.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道沙脊开始，落到餐桌旁一把空着的椅子。

normal.en: One s is enough for sand; the sweet one takes two.
normal.cn: 沙地一个 s 就够，甜点那个要两个 s。

normal.en: A desert is a place where even leaving leaves a mark.
normal.cn: 沙漠是连离开都会留下痕迹的地方。

normal.en: To desert a friend is to make a small desert of his room.
normal.cn: 抛弃一个朋友，就是把他的房间变成一小片荒漠。

normal.en: Wind works all day and builds only ridges.
normal.cn: 风忙了一整天，只堆出一道道沙脊。

normal.en: Empty land and empty promises share one word.
normal.cn: 空掉的土地与空掉的承诺，共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a boot print that the wind erases before dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个靴印在天黑前就被风抹掉。

abstract.en: Picture a table set for two with one chair pushed in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张为两个人摆好的桌子，一把椅子被推了回去。

abstract.en: Picture a road that stops where the sand begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路在沙地开始的地方断掉。

examples.en: Few plants can survive in the desert.
examples.cn: 很少植物能在沙漠里存活。

examples.en: He deserted his family and moved to another city.
examples.cn: 他抛弃了家人，搬到另一座城市。

examples.en: The village was quite deserted at noon.
examples.cn: 中午时村子里空无一人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desert 记成「得沙漠」：de 像「得」，sert 像「沙地」，走进去就只剩风和沙。

root: 来自拉丁语 desertum，源于 deserere（舍弃），由 de-（解除）与 serere（连接）构成。本义是被解开联结、丢空的地方，后来名词专指干旱的沙漠，动词则保留舍弃与擅离的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a dry plain nobody lives on, to a person left behind, to a duty dropped without leave.
sensesIntro.cn: 从无人居住的干旱平原，到被丢下的人，再到未经许可丢下的职守。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a place stripped of water and of people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被抽走水、也被抽走人的地方。

branches.en: The first sense is emptiness made of heat and sand.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是用炎热和沙堆出来的空。

branches.en: The second sense is emptiness made by a person walking away.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人走开所造成的空。

branches.en: The third sense is the empty post left at the gate.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是门口那个空掉的岗位。

branches.en: Land and people are called deserted by the same logic: no one is there.
branches.cn: 土地与人同样被说成荒废，理由一样：那里没有人。

branches.en: Leaving a friend and leaving a post both break a bond that should hold.
branches.cn: 丢下朋友与丢下岗哨，都断开了本该牵着的那根线。

intro.en: Desert grows a family about empty land and about people who leave their place.
intro.cn: desert 长出一族词，既关于空掉的土地，也关于离开原位的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin serere, to join, and de- undoes the joining, so deserere means to unjoin.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 serere（连接），de- 把这层连接解开，deserere 就是使分离。

items.meaning: to leave behind, or dry empty land
items.example: They crossed the desert by night.

items.meaning: the act of abandoning a duty
items.exampleCN: 擅离职守曾是很重的罪。

items.example: The deserter was caught at the border.
